title: Bipolar Disorder, Manic Episode
scenario: A 29-year-old male client is brought to the emergency department by his family after 5 days of not sleeping, rapid pressured speech, and reckless spending. He has a known diagnosis of bipolar I disorder and stopped taking lithium three weeks ago.

lines: 29-year-old male brought in by wife for escalating behavior over 5 days. Speech rapid, loud, and pressured; difficult to interrupt. Flight of ideas noted, jumping between topics. Reports sleeping about 2 hours per night and feeling 'better than ever.' Wife states he spent GHS 40000 on unneeded electronics this week. Grandiose statements about starting three businesses. Irritable when redirected. Stopped lithium 3 weeks ago because he 'felt fine.'

Client pacing the room, unable to sit for assessment. Intrusive toward other clients in the waiting area. Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation but is easily agitated. Placed in a low-stimulation room. IV access obtained; labs drawn including lithium level.
Provider notified of subtherapeutic lithium level. Orders received. Client remains highly distractible and has not eaten since arrival. One-to-one observation initiated for safety.

Client sleeping 6 hours overnight. Speech slower and easier to interrupt. Able to complete a full meal seated. Participated in a structured group activity without intrusiveness. Reports understanding the need to resume medication.
Lithium carbonate 300 mg PO three times daily (discontinued by client 3 weeks ago)
Admit to inpatient behavioral health unit, voluntary
Resume lithium carbonate 300 mg PO three times daily
Olanzapine 10 mg PO now for acute agitation
Offer high-calorie finger foods and fluids
Basic metabolic panel and renal function before dosing

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: Which 4 findings are consistent with an acute manic episode?

options.text: Rapid, pressured speech with flight of ideas

children.rationale: Decreased need for sleep, pressured speech with flight of ideas, impulsive spending, and grandiosity are hallmark features of mania. A normal drug screen and sodium are not manic findings.

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it reflects a psychological or a physiological/safety concern. Each finding may reflect more than one.
children.rationale: Flight of ideas and grandiosity are mood/thought disturbances. Severe sleep loss affects both mental state and physical safety. Not eating and a subtherapeutic lithium level are physiological concerns explaining the relapse.

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse identifies that the priority problem is {1}, and the most likely reason for this relapse is {2}.

choices.text: risk for injury related to hyperactivity and poor judgment

children.rationale: The client's hyperactivity, impulsivity, and impaired judgment create the greatest immediate danger, making risk for injury the priority. The subtherapeutic lithium level and reported nonadherence identify medication discontinuation as the cause; TSH and drug screen are normal.

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client during acute mania.

rows.text: Encourage participation in a large, competitive group game
Set firm, consistent limits on intrusive behavior
Confront the client's grandiose statements argumentatively

children.rationale: A calm environment, portable high-calorie foods, and consistent limit-setting support a manic client. Stimulating competitive activity and arguing over grandiose beliefs escalate agitation and are contraindicated.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: As lithium therapy is resumed, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Ensure adequate sodium and fluid intake
Teach the client the signs of lithium toxicity
Restrict all dietary sodium to zero
Withhold all food and fluids for 24 hours

children.rationale: Lithium requires level monitoring and stable sodium and fluid intake, and clients must learn toxicity signs. Restricting sodium raises lithium toward toxic levels, and withholding food and fluids is unsafe.

children.subject: Mental Health
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment plan has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Speech slower and easier to interrupt
Completing a full meal while seated
Pacing and unable to sit still

children.rationale: Restored sleep, organized speech, adequate intake, and appropriate social behavior show the mania is resolving. Continued pacing and restlessness would indicate ongoing mania, not improvement.
